key_insight: Pressure tunes ferroelectric LaMoN$_3$ from a 2.17 eV to 1.45 eV indirect-gap absorber while strengthening photovoltaic-relevant optical responses, with peak bulk photovoltaic performance near 15 GPa.
engineering_relevance: This suggests pressure-engineered nitride perovskite absorbers could be used to design multi-junction solar devices that separately optimize linear absorption and nonlinear shift-current generation.
method: First-principles DFT and DFPT to test structural and dynamical stability up to 40 GPa
Many-body G$_0$W$_0$ and BSE calculations to quantify bandgaps, excitons, and optical response
Tight-binding modeling to analyze pressure-dependent nonlinear photovoltaic currents
evidence_signal: The abstract reports pressure-dependent computed results showing a shrinking quasiparticle bandgap, improved SLME, reduced exciton binding energy, and a shift-current/bulk photovoltaic peak near 15 GPa.
watch_item: The implementation challenge is that the optimal pressure-dependent phases may be difficult to synthesize and maintain in practical devices, especially while preserving oxygen-free nitride stability.
paper_title: Harnessing Linear and Nonlinear Optical Responses in Ferroelectric LaMoN$_3$ for Enhanced Photovoltaic Efficiency
